title: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Benchmarking Rule Compliance under Agent Context Compaction
title_zh: 智能体还会遵守规则吗？智能体上下文压缩下的规则合规性基准测试

paragraphs.en: ARCBench基准揭示智能体上下文压缩后规则违规显著增加，即使规则被保留也无法保证合规。 LLM agents compact long histories to fit their context windows, but the compacted context must still carry the operating rules that govern later actions. Prior work shows that violations rise after compaction, but measures compliance outside a complete agent harness and does not identify where each violation comes from. We introduce ARCBench(Agent Rule Compliance Benchmark), a configurable benchmark built on the open-source pi agent harness. Its tool-calling agent loop lets us measure rule compliance from actions taken during execution, bringing the evaluation closer to deployed agent workflows. Using ARCBench, we examine where violations after compaction come from, and how different compaction configurations and adversarial settings change their sources. We find that compaction rarely deletes the rule: most violations after compaction occur while the rule is still in the compacted history, with the agent treating a later request as permission, ignoring the rule, and proceeding anyway. Where violations come from depends on the configuration: how the rule is delivered decides whether the agent would break it even without compaction, while the compaction strategy and budget decide whether the rule survives. The strongest compactor-targeted attack more than doubles violations by corrupting the rule in the summary and changing how the agents behave, whereas the strongest defense restores the rule in most summary but still violates. Finally, retaining a rule does not guarantee compliance: compacted runs that retain the rule violate more than twice as often as runs with the full history.
paragraphs.zh: ARCBench基准揭示智能体上下文压缩后规则违规显著增加，即使规则被保留也无法保证合规。大型语言模型智能体压缩长历史以适配其上下文窗口，但压缩后的上下文仍必须携带支配后续操作的运行规则。 已有工作表明压缩后违规会增加，但其在不完整的智能体框架之外度量合规性，且无法识别每次违规的来源。 我们提出ARCBench（智能体规则合规基准），这是一个构建在开源pi智能体框架之上的可配置基准。 其工具调用智能体循环使我们能够从执行期间采取的行动来度量规则合规性，使评估更贴近已部署的智能体工作流。 利用ARCBench，我们考察压缩后违规来自何处，以及不同的压缩配置和对抗性设置如何改变其来源。 我们发现压缩很少删除规则：压缩后的大多数违规发生在规则仍保留在压缩历史中的情况下，此时智能体将后续请求视为许可，忽视规则并继续执行。 违规来源取决于配置：规则的交付方式决定智能体即使在没有压缩的情况下是否也会违反规则，而压缩策略和预算则决定规则是否能存活下来。 最强的针对压缩器的攻击通过在摘要中破坏规则并改变智能体的行为方式，使违规增加了一倍以上；而最强的防御在大多数摘要中恢复了规则，但仍然存在违规。 最后，保留规则并不能保证合规：保留规则的压缩运行比拥有完整历史的运行违规频率高出两倍以上。
